# task-47b0cad2: copy the marked panel across a divided grid

## Rule
A grid is partitioned by full-width/full-height uniform divider bands into equal rectangular panels. Identify the unique panel containing the pattern/markers (cells different from the ordinary panel background); copy that panel's **entire contents**, including its background cells, into every panel at the same local coordinates. Keep divider lines unchanged. Do not assume the source is always the top-left panel: locate it from the current input.

## Evidence
- Demo (11x5): color-2 dividers are column 2 and rows 3,7. The resulting panels are 3x2. The upper-left panel `[[6,6],[8,1],[1,1]]` is copied into all six panels. This establishes copying the whole tile, not only the non-background markers.
- Solved test (17x11): color-4 dividers are columns 3,7 and rows 5,11. Panels are 5x3. The distinctive tile is the middle-left panel (rows 6-10, columns 0-2): `[[1,1,7],[9,1,1],[1,7,1],[1,1,1],[1,1,1]]`. Its complete 5x3 pattern was copied into each of the nine panels. A prior wrong guess left the marker tile unchanged; the actual operation replicates it throughout.

## Procedure
1. Find full uniform divider rows/columns and determine equal panel sizes.
2. Inspect panels and select the one with the non-background pattern; its position may vary. In known evidence all other panels are uniform background.
3. Tile the selected panel into every panel, preserving local coordinates and all cells, including background.
4. Preserve divider bands exactly; validate dimensions, alignment, and row widths.

## Additional confirmed test
- Solved 17x29 input with color-3 dividers at row 8 and columns 9, 19, yielding six 8x9 panels (3 columns x 2 rows). The unique source was the upper-left tile, with background 1 and markers `7` at local (0,0), `9` at (0,1), `7` at (2,2), and `0` at (3,5). Copying the entire 8x9 tile into each of the six panels while preserving all divider cells solved the test.

## Additional confirmed test
- Solved 13x15 input with divider row 6 and divider column 7, forming four 6x7 panels. The upper-left panel contained a 7-marker pattern on background 7; the lower-left and both right panels were otherwise blank. The complete upper-left tile was copied into all four panels, including filling the previously blank lower panels. Dividers remained 6. This confirms the source tile is replicated across both axes, even where the other panel positions initially contain only background.

## Additional confirmed test
- Solved a 13x23 input with a full color-8 divider at row 6 and full color-8 dividers at columns 7 and 15, creating six aligned 6x7 panels. The upper-left panel was the only one containing color-2 markers on color-3 background. Copy its full 6x7 contents into every panel, including the originally blank lower and right panels, preserving all divider lines. This confirms the rule also applies when only one panel contains the pattern and the panel's markers are sparse; copy all source-panel cells, not only color 2.

## Additional confirmed test
- Solved 11x15 input with color-1 divider row 5 and column 7, yielding four 5x7 panels. The unique source was the lower-right tile (rows 6-10, cols 8-14), copied in full into all four panels. Its exact local rows were `5555555`, `5255454`, `5555554`, `5555255`, `5565556` (background 5; marker colors 2, 4, 6). Preserve the divider row and column as 1. This confirms the source may be in the lower-right panel too.
- Transcription matters: an initial wrong answer shifted one color-6 marker from local column 2 to column 3 on the final tile row; the rule was right, but source coordinates must be copied exactly. Validate local row/column positions before replication.

## Caution
If multiple panels contain competing patterns, background is ambiguous, or panels differ in structure, do not blindly select a source; request a demo. This rule is task-specific and supported by multiple demos and correct test submissions.
